transcript.text: More than half of Massachusetts' races since 2014 have been completely uncontested. Think about that. When there's only one name on the ballot, there's no debate, no comparison, and no reason for anyone to earn your vote. Question 3 would put every candidate on one primary ballot, and the top finishers would move on to November. Every voter in every party, or none, gets a say. It's a simple change. More choices on the ballot and representatives who have to answer to all of us. Vote yes on question 3.

transcript.text: Flip a coin. That's your odds of your state legislative race actually being contested in Massachusetts since 2014. 51% of races in this state, more than half, have had just one name on the ballot. No opponent, no debate, no choice. Massachusetts ranks dead last in the country for electoral competitiveness. That's not democracy. That's your leaders being chosen for you. And it's not because good candidates don't exist, it's because the system makes it nearly impossible for a challenger to even get on the ballot in the first place. So voters show up to rubber stamp a decision that was already made for them.

result.summary: The video critiques Massachusetts's lack of competitive elections, highlighting that over half the races have no opposition, undermining democracy.
